chunks: "Did we not restrain you," they said, "from (entertaining) creatures from the outside world?"

key_terms.الْعَالَمِينَ: The worlds or creatures/beings (of the heavens)

ai.seo_question: What did the disbelievers ask Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding his claim of traveling to the heavens?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah Al-Isra, the disbelievers challenge Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by asking if they had not previously commanded him to stay away from the 'worlds' (al-'alamin), implying his claim of the Night Journey (Al-Isra) and Ascension (Al-Mi'raj) contradicted their prior instructions for him to remain grounded among them. Shia scholars often interpret 'al-'alamin' here as referring to the jinn or the general populace, highlighting the skepticism of the Quraych regarding his spiritual elevation and divine connection. This rhetorical question underscores the tension between the Prophet's unique spiritual status and the worldly expectations of his contemporaries.
